physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.title: Physical Realizability of a Proposition
physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.conceptual_definition: This logical statement asserts the existence of at least one physically possible world or state $w$ within the set of all physical worlds $W_{phys}$ for which the proposition $\psi$ holds true.
physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.intuitive_summary: This formula states that a given proposition or condition $\psi$ is physically realizable, meaning there is at least one physical scenario or state where it is true.
physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.interpretation: This statement is fundamental in the philosophy of physics and model theory, particularly when evaluating the consistency and predictive power of physical theories. It moves beyond mere logical possibility by restricting the domain of consideration to $W_{phys}$, the set of states or models that are consistent with the laws of physics. If this statement is true, it implies that the proposition $\psi$ is not physically impossible, and a physical configuration or process described by $\psi$ could, in principle, exist or occur. This has profound implications for experimental design, theoretical predictions, and the interpretation of physical phenomena, as it establishes whether a given state of affairs is within the realm of physical reality as defined by our current understanding of nature.
physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.symmetry_origin: This statement itself does not directly express a physical symmetry or conservation law. However, the definition and structure of the set $W_{phys}$ (the set of physically possible worlds) are implicitly constrained by the fundamental symmetries and conservation laws of the underlying physical theory. For a proposition $\psi$ to be physically realizable, it must be consistent with these symmetries, such as Lorentz invariance, gauge invariance, or the conservation laws derived from Noether's theorem. The existence of such a world $w$ implies that $\psi$ does not violate these foundational principles.
physical-realizability-of-a-proposition.limits_and_boundary: If the set of physically possible worlds $W_{phys}$ is empty (which would imply an inconsistent or ill-defined physical theory), then this statement is vacuously false for any proposition $\psi$. If $\psi$ is a logical contradiction, then $w \vDash \psi$ is never true for any $w$, and thus the statement $\exists w \in W_{phys}: w \vDash \psi$ is false. Conversely, if $\psi$ is a logical tautology, and $W_{phys}$ is non-empty, then the statement is true. This statement also contrasts with universal quantification, $\forall w \in W_{phys}: w \vDash \psi$, which would assert the physical necessity of $\psi$.

w.name: World or State
w.description: A specific physically possible world, state, or model instance within the set $W_{phys}$.

W_{phys}.name: Set of Physical Worlds
W_{phys}.description: The set of all physically possible worlds, states, or models consistent with a given physical theory or set of axioms.

\\psi.name: Proposition or Formula
\\psi.description: A logical proposition, statement, or formula whose truth value is being evaluated within a world $w$.
